## Taxonomic scope

::: {.vm-section}
VirMarkDB is a curated reference database of viral marker-gene sequences. The current release covers **Nucleocytoviricota** within **Bamfordvirae**, with taxonomy derived from the **ICTV Virus Metadata Resource ([VMR_MSL41.v1.20260320](https://ictv.global/sites/default/files/VMR/VMR_MSL41.v1.20260320.xlsx))**.

::: {.text-center}
[![](assets/ictv_logo.png){fig-alt="ICTV logo" width="120"}](https://ictv.global/)
:::

| Rank | Value |
|---|---|
| Kingdom | Bamfordvirae |
| Phylum | Nucleocytoviricota |
| Source | [ICTV](https://ictv.global/) [VMR_MSL41.v1.20260320](https://ictv.global/sites/default/files/VMR/VMR_MSL41.v1.20260320.xlsx) |

Taxonomy from Kingdom to Species is derived from the ICTV VMR. Manual genome additions follow the same taxonomy fields.
:::


## Marker genes

::: {.vm-section}
The current release includes eight conserved marker genes for Nucleocytoviricota.

<div class="marker-list">
<span class="marker">majorcapsid</span>
<span class="marker">dnapol</span>
<span class="marker">atpase</span>
<span class="marker">primase</span>
<span class="marker">rnapol1</span>
<span class="marker">rnapol2</span>
<span class="marker">tf2s</span>
<span class="marker">vltf3</span>
</div>

| Marker | Description |
|:---:|---|
| `majorcapsid` | Major capsid protein (MCP) |
| `dnapol` | DNA polymerase B |
| `atpase` | Packaging ATPase |
| `primase` | Primase |
| `rnapol1` | RNA polymerase subunit 1 |
| `rnapol2` | RNA polymerase subunit 2 |
| `tf2s` | Transcription factor S-II / TFIIS-like |
| `vltf3` | Viral late transcription factor 3 |

:::

## Lineage-specific markers and HMM profiles

::: {.vm-section}
Some viral marker genes are too divergent to be represented by a single **HMM profile** across all viral lineages. In addition, not all **marker genes** are relevant for all taxonomic groups. For this reason, **VirMarkDB** uses marker groups to associate **marker genes** with specific viral lineages and **dedicated HMM profiles**.

Each marker group links:
1. a marker gene;
2. a viral lineage or taxonomic group;
3. a reference protein set;
4. the HMM profile built from this reference set.

More details on [Workflow](workflow.qmd) page.

This structure allows **VirMarkDB** to build separate HMM profiles for divergent lineages while keeping a common marker-gene framework across the database.

:::


## Output files and formats

::: {.vm-section}

::: {.vm-subsection}
<div class="vm-subtitle">Release archive structure</div>


The public release is distributed as a versioned archive. See [Releases](releases.qmd) for download links.

```text
VirMarkDB_vX.Y.Z/
├── markers/
├── virus_informations/
├── README.md
├── CITATION.cff
├── LICENSE
└── CHANGELOG.md
```
:::

::: {.vm-subsection}
<div class="vm-subtitle">Markers</div>
Organised by taxonomic group and marker:
```text
markers/<group_id>/<marker>/
``` 

| File | Description |
|---|---|
| `<marker_group_id>_protein.fasta` | Protein sequences of the retained ORFs |
| `<marker_group_id>_nucleotide.fasta` | Nucleotide sequences of the retained ORFs |
| `<marker_group_id>_virus_orf_description.tsv` | Per-ORF table with HMM hit metrics and virus metadata |

**Protein FASTA header**

```
>orf_name marker Kingdom;Phylum;Class;Order;Family;Genus;Species
```

**ORF description table**

| Column | Description |
|:---:|---|
| `orf_name` | ORF identifier from Prodigal |
| `virus_id` | Genome identifier |
| `marker` | Marker name |
| `copy_rank` | Rank among hits for the same genome and marker group |
| `evalue` | HMMER e-value |
| `score` | HMMER bit score |
| `score_ratio` | ORF score / best score for this genome × marker group |
| `length_ratio` | ORF length / best ORF length for this genome × marker group |

:::

::: {.vm-subsection}
<div class="vm-subtitle">Virus_informations</div>

| File | Description |
|---|---|
| `virus_compo_taxo.tsv` | Wide-format table: one row per genome, one column per marker group |
| `virus_metadata.tsv` | Genome-level metadata: identifiers, virus names, host source, taxonomy |

:::

:::

::: {.callout-important}
Missing values do not automatically indicate true biological absence. They may reflect incomplete genome sequences, marker divergence, ORF prediction limits or filtering thresholds. See [About — limitations](about.qmd#notes-and-limitations) for details.
